chapter_title: Concerning the Three Blows that befell the Enemy b
spiritual_reading:
The very principle of denial, which resists the Divine, has been struck by a complete series of defeats through the full descent of wisdom, and in each of these it has met increasingly decisive states of peril from that wisdom.

First, it was drawn out from its obscured ultimates into a state where it could be exposed in the open of spiritual discernment, and it was cut off from the ultimate falsities in which it had taken its footing. In that first combat it was overcome, restrained, and held fast by the living reception of good and truth in the human mind.

The second defeat is the state when its coherence is undone: its congealed persuasions are loosened, its fixed form is dispersed, and it perishes by the burning out of self-love under the presence of Divine love. It is ruined and cast down because the fabricated appearances by which it had subsisted are taken away. Then it is drawn together into the lasting restraint that fits its own inmost pattern, and it is reduced to the same powerless condition it had at the first emergence of its evil.

The third defeat that comes upon this resisting principle is the final reversal at the completion, when all things are discriminated and set in order, and what is active and ruling in evil is severed from what is receptive and fostering in it. Then the ruling falsity is confined in a hardened, undivided compulsion, while the receptive element is shut up in utter spiritual death. Between them there is established an unremovable separation, an immutable barrier fixed in the midst, through successive states without end.

This, then, is how the perpetual restraint of that resisting principle is effected: by a confinement heavy with its own evil and made firm by Divine order, from which there is no release, because its restraint is fully accomplished and confirmed to eternity. Its removal from all mingling with the good is likewise fully accomplished, and that separation stands to eternity.

fills.notes: The first war ends in restraint by the Living Soul: the enemy is seized, restrained, held fast. “Bound” matches the substrate register of fettering and capture.

The second blow culminates in being “gathered” into a fetter that corresponds to his own archetypal pattern. The directional movement is into confinement; “to the fetter” is the demanded construction.
The ‘rolling back’ is specified as occurring at the completion of the cycle; “at the end” is the fixed eschatological marker in this substrate’s impersonal cosmology.
The separation is a discrimination of active from receptive within evil (male from female). The required preposition is the one of severance: “divided from”.

Opposition of outcomes: the male is “bound” (constrained in a lump); the female is not merely placed but cast into a tomb-like shutness. “Thrown into the tomb” preserves the harsh, impersonal finality of the substrate image.

fills.fill: and be divided apart, and be set apart
fills.notes: The sense demands an absolute, irreversible separation established by a barrier: not a mere physical stone, but a fixed partition ‘in their midst’ across successive generations. The restored verbs make explicit the decisive severing that the great stone effects.

The close is a confirmation formula: the powers of Light have fully effected the binding and separation ‘for ever’. “They have achieved” preserves the accomplished, juridical-cosmic tone rather than devotional language.

assessment: Most lacunae are tightly constrained by the chapter’s fixed three-stage defeat pattern (exposure and capture, dissolution and consolidation into a fitting fetter, final separation and irreversible partition). Only ¶4 #4 is genuinely open-ended because the surviving syntax allows several equivalent ways to express the same correspondential requirement (an unremovable separation established by the great stone).
